hook: The 13th century Poetic Edda split the entire cosmos into 9 realms.

sections.voiceover: The 13th century Poetic Edda split the entire cosmos into 9 realms.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of an illuminated 13th-century Icelandic manuscript page showing ancient Old Norse runes.
sections.sfx_cue: Deep parchment rustle with low cinematic sub-bass drone

sections.voiceover: In the 13th century, Snorri Sturluson compiled oral poems into the Prose Edda. What structural role did the world-tree Yggdrasil play in anchoring these 9 distinct realms?
sections.visual_cue: Historical illustration of compiler Snorri Sturluson writing, shifting to an intricate cosmological diagram of Yggdrasil.
sections.sfx_cue: Soft quill scratching transitioning to wind rushing through distant branches

sections.voiceover: However, scholar John Lindow notes that the cosmos faced constant threats from giants and gods.
sections.visual_cue: Dramatic historical artwork depicting ancient mythological giants surrounding the cosmic boundaries.
sections.sfx_cue: Low ominous brass hit with heavy reverberating thud

sections.voiceover: Yggdrasil physically supported all 9 realms, including divine Asgard and the home of the elves. Sturluson authored the Prose Edda, which serves as the primary structural source for these realms.
sections.visual_cue: Sweeping cinematic view across a medieval parchment map detailing Asgard, Alfheim, and the trunk of Yggdrasil.
sections.sfx_cue: Ethereal atmospheric drone swelling to a decisive musical strike

sections.voiceover: 9 realms remained bound together by the world-tree Yggdrasil.
sections.visual_cue: Centred depiction of the great ash tree Yggdrasil with all branches connecting the outer realms.
